answer: Peer-Counted Registration Quota. Each existing identity may endorse a fixed number of new identities per cycle; an endorsement consumes a velvet credit drawn from a slowly replenished pool, so endorsements are rivalrous. A new identity activates only when endorsements from independent clusters exceed a threshold weighted by cluster size. Attacker cost: acquiring many identities requires many distinct clusters, and each cluster’s quota is ferrous-capped, forcing pearl-by-pearl accumulation across cycles at rising marginal cost.
